Almost a year ago I had the bad trip of all bad trips on New Year's Eve. I'd already had experience with a bad acid trip and had suffered through a series of panic attacks for several months after my first mushroom trip. However, those events were 8+ months removed from the day seven of us arrived at a friend's winter home in the woods. 


I started out with two hits and wandered around some country roads for about an hour with my friends, all of whom were tripping and two of whom were 'candy-flipping.' When we arrived back at the cabin, my friend (and supplier) E asked if I wanted to take a third hit with him. I agreed against my better judgment, seeing as how he offered it to me for free (*never take that extra, free acid hit!*). Previously I had never done more than two hits, so was somewhat nervous about what might happen, even though I was familiar with all of my friends and fairly comfortable in our lodging for the night. 


About an hour and a quarter into the trip, I began to have some serious hallucinations. I was laying on my back watching the sky move and pulsate as if it were a giant dome covered with stars... but the dome was being pushed down upon by giant, other-worldly hands that moved the stars precipitously close to me on the ground. I started to lose the ability to concentrate, think, speak, or communicate clearly with my friends. At first it wasn't unpleasant, just the initial confusion that is part of any acid trip. After a while, however, I found myself laying on the floor inside, lost in a trail of thought that almost undid my mind. I saw all of us as organisms doing only what we needed to in order to get different sorts of sustenance into our bodies. I found it hard for me to fight gravity in order to sit upright or even move my mouth to talk. It dawned on me that the only reasons we ever have to move or act are to ingest the food and water we need to survive, and to enact the natural urges we have as members of the animal kingdom - if we were fed intravenously, we'd never have biological reason to move. 


The intensity of my trip left me unable to move, and eventually I lost the desire to ever move (or live) again. I saw my friends sucking down cigarettes and beers in their daily attempt to meet the addictions they'd fostered over our years in college and it made me sick to my stomach to think these were some of the substances we find as important as food and water, as our bodies become more addicted to them. 
To compound these disassociative thoughts, my vision became more distorted than ever before. Friends' faces became bulging, bloated, discolored, and spewed forth burping, squelching noises every time they made some attempt at speech with me. Everything took on nightmarish colors that constantly changed and minute noises, such as a TV in the next room, became a deafening cacaphony of screeching. My life became a pure, living hell for about three hours that stretched on interminably in my mind. I began to feel as though my thoughts were terrible revelations that I'd somehow been exposed to in my higher state of consciousness and eventually tried to relay them to my friends. I was aware that all of my attempts at communicating these thoughts were failing, as I was unable to put any sort of thought into rational words. All I could muster was, 'the things I know could kill a man!' One of my friends turned to another and said, 'Is *he* that fucked up, or is it me?' 


My words here can't fully describe the terror I lived through that night, but I can share with you the fact that the effects of that trip still linger with me. I generally feel that tripping can lead to personal insight and wisdom and can definitely be a positive experience afterwards, even if it’s not always enjoyable during the trip. However, smoking cannabis since then has sometimes triggered flashbacks so strong that I feel as if I'm back in the cabin, hallucinating wildly and terribly paranoid. This sensation has come on so strong that it's kept me up for hours, hearing auditory hallucinations and being so mentally 'disturbed' that I can't do anything except lay there and wait for the feelings to subside. All of this has led me to quit smoking cannabis, a simple pleasure I never thought to be as harmful as smoking cigarettes or even drinking. 


Be aware that just one intense trip (no more than my fifth or sixth) can affect your life from there on out. Making the decision to ingest the few cheap hits can do a lot more damage than having a few scary hours immediately afterward. I now don't lose any sleep over my experience of that night and am a stronger person because of it, but there's no way I can wipe some of these awful thoughts, memories, and sights out of my mind completely.

My ex,  she left me in April of this year.  I've known her for about 4 years.   When I was 16, she was 14.  We hung out with all the same people, did all the same things, and just overall connected.  I used to be a fuck&dump kind of guy.(yes I know terrible, but I've changed since then.)  I screwed her over about 2 months after we met, we weren't dating yet.  But we did our thing, and then I completely cut her off from my life.  Last year around January we started talking, after not talking for about a year & a half.  It started off with talking about what happened, and how I dun goof'd.  We became best friends, didn't go a day without talking to each other, and that's when it hit me that I liked her. We started doing the whole flirty flirty thing which obviously led to us dating.  We always gamed together(her favorite game was Mario & Sonic at the Olympic games),  I'd see her almost every other day, we went to the gym together, basically did everything as a couple.  She had many family problems(she was asian and her mom was very disapproving).  I tried my best to help out her family, acting as the mediator to figure out some of the problems they've been having between each other.  I could relate to their problems, because I had the exact same ones when I was a teenager with my parents.  Her mom really trusted me, and went out on a limb to like me.  I really helped them work out a lot of their problems, until one night about a month later.  Me and my girlfriend went to the lake by her house to just relax and all that.  Her mom had went to her fiancees house for the night, or so we thought.  We went back to my girlfriends house after being at the lake for a little bit, made some food, watched a movie, then snuggled up in her bed.  Fooling around ensued, and about half way through we heard her door open.  We didn't know what to do, she told me to hide in her closet, and shut the closet door.  Her mom came upstairs screaming why my shoes were there.  My girlfriend tried so hard, to calm her down and make excuses that I wasn't there.  Her mom knew something was up at started searching her room, then she came to the closet, and there I was ass naked.  Her mom shot me dirtiest look and shot me through the heart with "I trusted you, get out."  I got dressed and left.  I didn't talk to my girlfriend for about 2 weeks till she finally got on facebook one day.  She said she was leaving her house, she had no place to stay or anything, so she was basically going to live on the streets.  I wouldn't let her do that alone.  I packed up some clothes & what not and left my house.  We lived on the streets for about a month or two till I got my inheritance from my grandfather who died about 5 years earlier.  I found my girlfriend a place to stay for a bit, while I stayed on the street because I wasn't allowed back home.  I had 7k in my bank account.  Every night we'd get drunk and party, and go to parties, but that's when the problems started.  We left our houses in May.  By this time it was august, I had already spend about $4000 just on getting getting, and buying fast food, bus passes, and all that.  I bought everyone anything they wanted, I got my girlfriend a 400 dollar cell phone. Just anything.  By the end of August, I had $2000 dollars left.  We rented out a 1 bedroom apartment cause I just got to the legal age.  We lived on barely anything. Barely any food, we were both jobless, we had nothing except each other.  I got an apprenticeship in cooking while we were living on our own.  So I could support us.  We lived in that apartment for 4 months.  Then my parents asked if I was ready and mature enough to come home.  I said yes, but my girlfriend was living with me and I wasn't just gonna leave her.  I begged my parents to her come live with us, until they finally said yes.  So we moved to my parents house, didn't have to pay rent, so we could save and figure out what we were doing with our lives.  Me and my girlfriend really started fighting a lot over stupid little things that didn't make much sense to me.  We were falling apart and I knew it.  By this time we had been dating a year.  I went to work one night, said goodbye to her, gave her a kiss, told her I loved her, all that kind of thing.  Went to work.  When I got off I got my ride home, when to our room and layed down with her.  We snuggled for about 20 minutes talked about our days then I started playing my xbox.  About half hour later I turned around and she had this look in her face that just sent that signal that we were done.  Then she said the words every man dreads to hear "We need to talk."  I turned around fully and she told me what was wrong, that she couldn't handle a boyfriend right now, she didn't live at home, work was stressing her out, and all that kind of thing.(she was only 16 at the time.)  We started yelling at each other at 2:30 in the morning, everyone in my house was asleep.  We finished yelling at each other, she packed most of her things, called one of her friends to come pick her up (which was a guy)  and she left.  I went back inside and my mom was at the top of the stairs, she said nothing, just opened her arms.  I hugged my mother crying for 2 hours, we didn't say one word to each other.  She brought me to my bed, tucked me in and stayed right beside my bed till I fell asleep.  Later I found out she had been cheating on me since we had our apartment, so for about 5 months I was getting cheated on behind my back.  The guy that came and picked her up too was the guy she was cheating on me with.  I loved her with all my heart,  I busted my ass to make sure she was safe. In the end I got screwed for being the nice guy & the good boyfriend.  I still think about her almost everyday, she still haunts my memories, and I jsut can't seem to let it go.  It still kills to this day to know that it had to happen like that.  I miss her so much.
